top_categories.workout_context: 7,615ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
121ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Bogota's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
At GFNY Bogota, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
7,615ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
GFNY Bogota's paved Colombian mountain roads with sustained forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 62 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Bogota. Train it until it feels boring.
62 miles on paved Colombian mountain roads with sustained burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Base fitness for GFNY Bogota. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
Low-cadence force work for 7,615ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on paved Colombian mountain roads with sustained. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At GFNY Bogota, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for GFNY Bogota’s 62 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.altitude: GFNY Bogota with 7,615ft of climbing, much of it above 8,000ft demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%. Altitude: 2,650m at the start, racing above 3,000m — oxygen availability is 73-75% of sea level; Temperature swings: cold starts (8-10C) in the salt mines, mild at valley floor, cold again at summit.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, TT Threshold, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 62 miles of paved colombian mountain roads with sustained climbing at extreme altitude in Zipaquira, Cundinamarca, Colombia.
